text:
maria: FYI discovered glibc 2.31 vuln flagged by SCA scanner in our base image. we should schedule a rebuild and ensure KMS signing + audit hooks are in place.

tyler: ack. which image tag is affected? staging or all?

maria: both staging/base:2023-06 and prod/base:2023-03. severity P1 for us because runtime containers pull base at deploy.

janet: oncall ping @kevin — can you own the rebuild window + canary? also need RBAC check for the keystore signer role.

kevin: i'll take lead. tentative plan: 1) rebuild minimal base with patched glibc, 2) run unitary smoke + vuln scan, 3) cosign sign with KMS, 4) rolling canary deploy to staging, 5) promote.

maria: add audit log hooks in the CI so every sign operation gets an entry to our audit cluster + retention tag. we had a gap last rotation.

tyler: for RBAC: current signer principal is service-account:imagesigner@infra. We need to restrict keystore decrypt to signer only (no admin console access). propose binding: 

```
# IAM excerpt
role: roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier
members:
  - serviceAccount:imagesigner@infra
conditions:
  - expr: request.time < timestamp("2025-01-01T00:00:00Z")
```

kevin: question — our cosign flow uses KMS asymmetric signing. will the new policy break existing ephemeral key wraps used in dedicated builds?

janet: good call. build-bot uses ephemeral wrapped keys via the keystore bridge. need to add a short-lived grant for the builder SA during the build step then revoke. can we do a preflight script?

kevin: yes. sample workflow: exchange wrapped key via KMS `GenerateAccessToken` + short TTL, run sign, then call `revokeGrant` in post step. I'll draft the script.

maria: also want audit entries in the image metadata: add annotation `signed-by:kms://projects/foo/locations/global/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/k/cryptoKeyVersions/1` and `signature-checksum` so infra can validate provenance at deploy.

tyler: on vuln triage: open a quick RFC for image pinning to explicit glibc patches and a monthly rebuild cadence. we shouldn't rely on ad-hoc hotpatches.

janet: incident-response note: if a CVE hit runtime in prod, fallback policy should replace exec with a lower-privilege variant and redirect traffic to the non-affected model pool. add to runbook.

kevin: scheduling: canary window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. I'll post PR with the build script + IAM delta. tagging @build-bot to trigger a dry-run.

build-bot: dry-run started for job images/rebase-glibc-2023-06-dryrun id=ci-3384. logs: https://ci.internal/reports/ci-3384

maria: thanks. once PR is up include the exact audit sink config (stackdriver filter + retention) and a helix ticket for compliance so they can sign off on the KMS policy change.

tyler: checklist for PR: - updated base Dockerfile (no extra packages) - SBOM updated - vuln scan baseline attached - cosign hook using KMS - IAM binding delta file - pre/post build grant script - audit sink config - rollback playbook snippet

kevin: i'll include all that. janet can you review RBAC snippet before I open?

janet: will do. quick comment: ensure the build-bot token has no iam.roles.grant privilege; use a separate short-lived grant flow instead of granting wide permissions to build-bot.

maria: perfect. after canary, we want an emergency rollback trigger in the deploy pipeline that will: patch image tag -> redeploy -> notify slack #incidents with summary. add a deploy-bot hook.

kevin: noted. drafting PR now, ETA 3h.

maria: great — post the PR link here and I'll kick off compliance review. :thumbsup:
